title: retries backoff idempotency circuit breakers and rate limits
concepts: Resilience strategies address different failure behaviors: timeout bounds waiting, retry repeats a potentially transient operation, circuit breaker stops calls likely to fail, bulkhead limits shared-resource impact, and rate limiting controls admission or request rate.

A retry is safe only when the operation is repeatable or deduplicated and the failure is plausibly transient. Retrying after an ambiguous response may repeat a side effect, while nested retries can multiply load and cause a retry storm.

Backoff with bounded attempts and jitter spreads retry pressure; respect server back-pressure such as Retry-After. A retry budget or deadline prevents unbounded retry work from consuming capacity and user time.

A circuit breaker observes failures over a defined window and moves through closed, open, and half-open behavior to reduce work against an impaired dependency. Its thresholds, sampling, fallback, and recovery probes must match the dependency and workload.

Rate limiting and concurrency limiting are related but distinct controls: one governs admissions over time, while the other caps simultaneous in-flight work. Bulkheads isolate capacity pools so one failing workload cannot consume every shared resource.

Timeouts, retries, hedging, breakers, bulkheads, rate limits, and fallbacks compose into a policy pipeline. Order changes behavior, so make cancellation propagation, overall deadline, retry eligibility, telemetry, and overload response explicit.

items: The current Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience API provides a standard HTTP resilience handler and configurable pipeline strategies; defaults are package-version-specific and should be read from the exact installed package documentation rather than frozen as timeless behavior.

scopeExclusions: Message-queue redelivery, broker dead-letter policies, and product-specific delivery retries (t08-008)
Transactional outbox/inbox and saga recovery coordination (t08-010)
HTTP method semantics and client protocol methods apart from the Retry-After boundary (t08-007)
Exact runtime APIs and package methods are addressed in the relevant language/framework track; this manifest covers named patterns and policy behavior
Retries do not guarantee eventual success, exactly-once effects, or safety for non-idempotent operations
Rate-limit algorithms are named for conceptual understanding; distributed synchronization and vendor-specific quota implementation are excluded
